_comment: Taxonomic class -> NCBI mitochondrial genetic code (translation table).
Single source of truth, read by BOTH lib/InvertTaxonGroups.groovy (which
prepare_samplesheet uses to resolve meta.genetic_code) and
bin/create_samplesheet.py (which writes the resolved code into the
samplesheet's genetic_code column). It exists because those two are a Groovy
set and a Python set that would otherwise drift -- the same failure that had
four copies of REF_GENES disagreeing before bin/mito_gene_order.py.
Class names are lowercase; both readers normalise before lookup.
A class that is NOT here and NOT in 'ambiguous' aborts the run rather than
taking a default. A wrong translation table mistranslates every CDS in the
annotation and surfaces as a terminal table2asn failure far from its cause,
so an unconfirmed class is worth stopping for. Add a class here once its code
is confirmed, or set the per-sample genetic_code samplesheet column, which
overrides this file.
'confidence' records how the code was established:
ncbi       - the group is named explicitly on NCBI's genetic code table,
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Utils/wprintgc.cgi
convention - the code is the standard one used for the group in published
mitogenomes, but NCBI's table does not name the group. Review
these before trusting them on a new lineage; moving one into
'ambiguous' is the safe direction.

codes.basis: NCBI table 4 (Mold, Protozoan, and Coelenterate Mitochondrial Code) gives its metazoan scope verbatim as 'Coelenterata (Ctenophora and Cnidaria)'.

Porifera is not named on NCBI's table 4 page, but NCBI's taxonomy assigns sponges mitochondrial code 4 and sponge mitogenomes are annotated under it. Sponges also share the reduced/atypical tRNA complement that puts them with Cnidaria in InvertTaxonGroups.REDUCED_TRNA_CLASSES.

NCBI table 5 (Invertebrate Mitochondrial Code) names Mollusca (Bivalvia; Polyplacophora), Arthropoda (Crustacea, Insecta) and Nematoda (Ascaris, Caenorhabditis). Annelida is the standard code-5 lophotrochozoan alongside them.

Minor invertebrate phyla not named on NCBI's table page. Published mitogenomes for each use the standard Invertebrate code, but none of these has been checked against a sample in this pipeline. Enteropneusta is listed here and NOT with the rest of Hemichordata: its sister class Pterobranchia is genuinely ambiguous (see below).

NCBI table 9 (Echinoderm and Flatworm) names 'Asterozoa (starfishes); Echinozoa (sea urchins); Rhabditophora among the Platyhelminthes'. Ophiuroidea is Asterozoa and Holothuroidea is Echinozoa. Crinoidea is neither, but published crinoid mitogenomes use the same code. Turbellaria is the old free-living-flatworm grouping, effectively Rhabditophora.

NCBI table 13 (Ascidian Mitochondrial Code) scope is 'Urochordata (tunicates)', evidenced from Pyura stolonifera, Halocynthia roretzi and Ciona savignyi. Tunicates sit inside Chordata but do not use the vertebrate code.

ambiguous.pterobranchia: Contains both Rhabdopleuridae (NCBI table 24) and Cephalodiscidae (table 33). The code cannot be resolved at class rank -- set the per-sample genetic_code column from the family.
ambiguous.hemichordata: Phylum rank spans Enteropneusta (code 5) and Pterobranchia (24 or 33). Resolve the sample to a class, or set the genetic_code column.
ambiguous.trematoda: NCBI has table 21 (Trematode Mitochondrial Code) specifically for Trematoda, and table 14 (Alternative Flatworm) for others. Table 9 covers only Rhabditophora among the flatworms, so 9 is not safe here.
ambiguous.cestoda: Neodermatan flatworm outside table 9's stated Rhabditophora scope; reported under both table 9 and table 14 in the literature.
ambiguous.monogenea: As cestoda -- outside table 9's stated scope, with table 14 reported for some lineages.
ambiguous.platyhelminthes: Phylum rank spans Rhabditophora (code 9) and the neodermatans above (9, 14 or 21). Resolve the sample to a class.
ambiguous.placozoa: Plausibly code 4 alongside the other basal metazoans, but not documented on NCBI's table page and never yet seen in a run.
